brand_names: Stalevo (combination product with levodopa and carbidopa)
purpose: Entacapone is used to help treat Parkinson's disease. It is always used together with levodopa and carbidopa — never alone. It helps reduce the 'wearing off' periods when your Parkinson's symptoms come back before your next dose of levodopa is due.
how_it_works: Your body normally breaks down levodopa (your main Parkinson's medication) too quickly before it can get into your brain and do its job. Entacapone blocks an enzyme called COMT that breaks levodopa down. By blocking this enzyme, entacapone helps levodopa last longer in your body so your brain gets more of it for a longer time.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, diarrhea, stomach pain, and a harmless brownish-orange discoloration of your urine — don't be alarmed if you notice this! You may also notice more uncontrolled movements (called dyskinesia), dizziness, or feeling more tired than usual.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you notice any sudden urge to sleep during the day, unusual behaviors like compulsive gambling or eating, or signs of a rare but serious condition called neuroleptic malignant syndrome (such as high fever, muscle stiffness, or confusion). Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor first. Also let your doctor know if you have liver problems, as this medication may not be safe for you.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 200 mg tablet taken by mouth with each dose of your levodopa/carbidopa medication. Most people take it 3 to 8 times per day depending on how often they take their levodopa. Always take it at the same time as your levodopa — not separately.
